answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 238 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the garden seed, the vertex timing is verifiable from the jetty record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 51 keys therefore pays 51 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
